intended_object: The antipode of the symmetric algebra Sym_K(M), seen as a Hopf algebra with primitive generators. It is the K-algebra endomorphism sending each generator ι(x) to −ι(x), i.e. Sym(−id_M). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `HopfAlgebra.ofAlgHom`.
explanation:
The body is `lift (-ι K M)`. By the universal property of the symmetric algebra, this is the unique K-algebra map into the commutative algebra Sym_K(M) that sends ι(x) to −ι(x), which is exactly the antipode.

Generality: K must be a commutative ring rather than a semiring, because the negation is taken in the target algebra; without additive inverses there is no antipode. M is only required to be an additive commutative monoid, which is the most general choice and avoids needing −id on M. This matches Mathlib's bialgebra structure on `SymmetricAlgebra`, which is stated over `CommSemiring R` with `AddCommMonoid M`.

Mathlib has the bialgebra structure on the symmetric algebra but no antipode or Hopf algebra instance for it, so there is no existing counterpart. When M is an additive group, `SymmetricAlgebra.map (-LinearMap.id)` would give the same map, but that is less general and not a separate named definition.
